answer: Randomness-gated activation lottery. Each new agent identity draws a slot from a verifiable random beacon tied to a future block, so slots cannot be precomputed or hoarded. An identity activates only when its drawn block index lands on a kernel bit that differs from all prior winners in that epoch. Attackers flooding N identities must wait out the beacon and accept low hit rates; each failed draw consumes a fixed per-identity entry cost plus idle time, and a velvet audit trail records draws so duplicates cluster visibly. Walnut-seeded epochs rotate, forcing repeated payment per attempt.
